claims.text: Ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder forms a simple BCC solid solution.
SPS at 1000 °C produces a dense MgAlTiVFeCo microstructure.
SPS at 1000 °C produces uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases.
The oxide barrier phases enhance mechanical strength relative to lower-temperature sintering.
The oxide barrier phases enhance corrosion resistance relative to lower-temperature sintering.
The oxide barrier phases enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to lower-temperature sintering.
High temperature and pressure during SPS promote diffusion sufficient for densification.
High temperature and pressure during SPS promote oxide precipitate formation.
The precipitates coalesce into continuous barrier phases.
The continuous barrier phases form a passive film resistant to chloride-ion penetration.
Resistance to chloride-ion penetration increases corrosion resistance.
Oxidation at 900 °C follows diffusion-controlled parabolic kinetics with biphasic growth.
The alloy sintered at 1000 °C will have approximately 96.7% relative density.
The alloy sintered at 1000 °C will have microhardness of approximately 1235.5 HV.
Relative to samples sintered at 850–950 °C, the 1000 °C sample will have a more positive corrosion potential and lower corrosion current density.
Samples sintered at 850–950 °C have lower relative density, reduced hardness, and poorer corrosion and oxidation resistance because barrier phases form incompletely.
Sintering above 1000 °C may cause magnesium volatilization.
Sintering below 800 °C may not produce the required densification and barrier-phase formation.
